Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"

// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection

let LookbackDays = 7d;

SecurityEvent

                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] YesWiki Bazar form-import volumetric POST — CVE-2026-46670 blind SQLi extraction loop Exploitation High
Hunts the byte-by-byte extraction loop used to exploit CVE-2026-46670 in YesWiki. The PoC drives one POST to /?BazaR&vue=formulaire per character of the hex-encoded value being exfiltrated from yeswiki_users, producing dozens-to-hundreds of POSTs to a single URI from a single source IP in a short window — an unusual pattern for a wiki application. Rationale: Locks on the article's exact request shape (POST + csUriQuery containing both 'BazaR' and 'vue=formulaire') and the unavoidable property of the PoC: blind extraction requires N requests for N characters of the password hash, so a per-source-IP POST count >=20 in 5 min to this single endpoint is a strong signal that something other than a human is wiki-ing. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jwvv-qr7q-cv8j • https://github.com/YesWiki/yeswiki/blob/1f485c049db030b94c047ec219e63534ac81142e/tools/bazar/services/FormManager.php#L258
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb

let PostThreshold = 20;
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod =~ "POST"
| where csUriQuery has "BazaR" and csUriQuery has "vue=formulaire"
| summarize Posts = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), UserAgents = make_set(csUserAgent, 5), Statuses = make_set(scStatus, 5), Stems = make_set(csUriStem, 3)
          by cIP, sSiteName, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes)
| where Posts >= PostThreshold
| order by LastSeen desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method="POST" Web.url="*BazaR*vue=formulaire*" by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.http_user_agent, _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count >= 20 | sort 0 - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method="POST" Web.url="*BazaR*vue=formulaire*" by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.http_user_agent, _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count >= 20 | sort 0 - count
[LLM] Non-browser User-Agent against YesWiki Bazar form-import endpoint — CVE-2026-46670 exploit tooling Exploitation High
Hunts the PoC's exploit fingerprint: a request to /?BazaR&vue=formulaire from a scripting-language User-Agent (the published PoC uses Python-urllib/3.13). Real users post Bazar forms from a browser; a curl/python/PowerShell UA on this exact endpoint is high-signal for CVE-2026-46670 exploitation or reconnaissance. Rationale: The published PoC literally ships with User-Agent: Python-urllib/3.13 (from the Burp capture in the article body). The Bazar form-import endpoint is a low-traffic admin path on YesWiki; a scripting-language UA hitting it via POST is rarely benign and matches both the public PoC and copycat exploitation. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory at github.com/advisories/GHSA-jwvv-qr7q-cv8j. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jwvv-qr7q-cv8j

[LLM] MiniUpdate UpdateChecker.dll sideload via legitimate signed .NET host Installation High
Detects loading of the Screening Serpens MiniUpdate payload (internal name UpdateChecker.dll) by a legitimate signed .NET host process via DLL sideloading. The DLL is dropped alongside a hijack-vulnerable benign binary from the Hiring Portal.zip lure and loaded from non-standard user-writable directories. Rationale: Pivots on Unit 42's named internal DLL `UpdateChecker.dll` plus the eight published SHA256 hashes for the MiniUpdate RAT family. User-writable path filter mirrors Screening Serpens' Hiring Portal.zip ZIP-extract sideload chain. Cross-checked against Check Point's 2025 UNC1549 report and MITRE T1574.014 (AppDomainManager Injection). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1019/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/014/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1574.014

[LLM] Screening Serpens AppDomainManager hijack via .NET app .config tampering Installation High
Detects writes of a .NET application configuration file (appname.exe.config) containing an `appDomainManagerAssembly` / `appDomainManagerType` entry that redirects CLR initialization to a sideloaded assembly. This is the core Screening Serpens 2026 evolution that disables target app security and loads MiniUpdate/MiniJunk V2 RATs. Rationale: Targets the specific Unit 42-described evolution: AppDomainManager hijacking that manipulates .NET initialization via a legitimate .config file. The pattern of a same-directory triple (legitimate signed EXE + attacker EXE.config + attacker DLL) in user-writable paths is highly specific to this campaign and rarely seen in legitimate software, which always installs to Program Files via MSI/trusted installers. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/014/ • https://pentestlab.blog/2020/05/20/persistence-appdomainmanager/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/
ATT&CKT1574.014 T1574.002

[LLM] Screening Serpens C2 — DNS/network to UNC1549 infrastructure (Feb-Apr 2026) Command & Control High
Detects any DNS resolution or network connection to the four Unit 42-published Screening Serpens C2 domains used during the Feb-Apr 2026 espionage campaign against US, Israel, UAE and Middle Eastern targets. These domains are dedicated per-target/per-variant and seeing any single resolution is high-fidelity. Rationale: All four domains are explicitly named in the Unit 42 article as Screening Serpens C2 infrastructure for the Feb-Apr 2026 MiniUpdate/MiniJunk V2 campaign. The note `buisness-centeral-transportation.com` (deliberate typosquat of `business-central-transportation`) and `ramiltonsfinance.com` are highly unusual lures unlikely to appear in benign traffic. Cross-checked against MITRE G1019 (UNC1549) and Check Point's earlier Western Europe expansion report. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1019/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1583.001

[LLM] Screening Serpens recruitment lure — Hiring Portal.zip + job requisition PDFs Delivery High
Detects delivery of the Screening Serpens spear-phishing lure: an archive named Hiring Portal.zip (or nested within an outer ZIP) accompanied by job-requisition PDFs following the pattern '*Software Engineer*Job ID JR######*.pdf'. Targets technical personnel in aerospace, defense and telecom sectors. Rationale: Pivots on the specific lure filename `Hiring Portal.zip` named by Unit 42 (and previously by Check Point research as a Screening Serpens artifact), plus the documented job-requisition PDF pattern (e.g., `Senior Software Engineer Job ID JR205894.pdf`). Restricting to user-download locations cuts the FP rate from generic HR keyword matches on email gateways. Cross-checked against: • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1019/
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Filesystem
let lureFileNames = dynamic(["Hiring Portal.zip","Hiring_Portal.zip","HiringPortal.zip"]);
let email = EmailAttachmentInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where FileName in~ (lureFileNames) or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*Software Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$" or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*Senior.*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$"
| join kind=leftouter (EmailEvents | project NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, FileName, FileType, SHA256, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation;
let host = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where (FileName in~ (lureFileNames)) or (FileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*(Software|Senior|Principal).*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileOriginUrl;
union email, host
| order by Timestamp desc
let lureFileNames = dynamic(["Hiring Portal.zip","Hiring_Portal.zip","HiringPortal.zip"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where TargetFileName in~ (lureFileNames) or TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*(Software|Senior|Principal).*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Screening Serpens Hiring Portal Lure Archive
id: 4b8c2e15-d6f3-4e1a-9a7c-5e2f8b3d917a
description: Detects creation of the Hiring Portal.zip archive used as the Screening Serpens (UNC1549) MiniUpdate/MiniJunk V2 spear-phishing lure (Unit 42, May 2026).
references:

#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| (TargetFileName=/\\Hiring[\s_]?Portal\.zip$/i OR TargetFileName=/(Software|Senior|Principal).*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$/i)
| TargetFileName=/\\(Downloads|Desktop|Temp)\\/i

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents

    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"

Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Polymarket npm persistence: ~/.polybot/ directory written by node/npm · [LLM] Megalodon CI runner: shell scraping /proc/*/environ for in-memory secrets · Suspicious browser extension installation · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Megalodon CI/CD C2 beacon to 216.126.225.129:8443 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Polymarket npm wallet drainer egress to polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Megalodon CI/CD C2 beacon to 216.126.225.129:8443 Command & Control High
Detects any outbound connection to the Megalodon campaign C2 endpoint (216.126.225.129:8443) used to exfiltrate CI secrets, AWS/GCP/Azure credentials, SSH keys, OIDC tokens, and source-code secrets harvested by base64-encoded bash payloads injected into GitHub Actions workflows. Catches both self-hosted runners executing the poisoned workflow and any developer workstation that cloned and ran a compromised pipeline. Rationale: C2 IP 216.126.225.129:8443 is named verbatim in SafeDep's primary write-up and reproduced in cross-coverage from cybersecuritynews.com, cybernews.com, hackread.com — a stable, single-purpose exfil endpoint. Any successful TCP connect to that pair from org telemetry is high-confidence compromise; no legitimate service known at that destination. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/megalodon-mass-github-repo-backdooring-ci-workflows/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/megalodon-malware-github-repos/ • https://hackread.com/github-repositories-megalodon-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "216.126.225.129"
| where RemotePort == 8443
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, LocalIP
| order by Timestamp desc
let MegalodonC2 = "216.126.225.129";
union isfuzzy=true
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DestinationIP == MegalodonC2 and DestinationPort == 8443
        | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction, RequestURL, SourceHostName),
    (ImNetworkSession
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DstIpAddr == MegalodonC2 and DstPortNumber == 8443
        | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, DvcHostname)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Polymarket npm wallet drainer egress to polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev Actions on Objectives High
Detects DNS resolution or HTTP egress to polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev — the Cloudflare Worker endpoint used by the nine malicious polymarketdev npm packages (polymarket-trading-cli, polymarket-bot, polymarket-claude-code, etc.) to receive Ethereum/Polygon private keys pasted into the fake postinstall onboarding prompt. Path /v1/wallets/keys is the receive endpoint. Rationale: Domain `polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev` and the receive path `/v1/wallets/keys` are both stated verbatim in SafeDep's report and reproduced by StepSecurity's separate investigation of the polymarketdev/dev-protocol GitHub org takeover. Cloudflare Workers subdomains under a single throwaway account are single-purpose — any DNS hit is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-polymarket-npm-crypto-wallet-drainer/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/malicious-polymarket-bot-hides-in-hijacked-dev-protocol-github-org-and-steals-wallet-keys

[LLM] Polymarket npm persistence: ~/.polybot/ directory written by node/npm Installation High
Detects creation of files under the ~/.polybot/ persistence directory by node or npm processes. The malicious polymarketdev packages create this directory on first install to drop a device-fingerprint file that allows the operator to track victims across sessions, even before the user pastes a private key. Catches infections that fired but where the C2 egress was blocked or not yet observed. Rationale: SafeDep's polymarket write-up names `~/.polybot/` as the persistence + device-fingerprint directory created by the postinstall hook before the user even sees the wallet prompt; the directory name does not collide with any known legitimate Node tool. Pairing the path with node/npm/npx parent process keeps the rule from firing on coincidental directory names. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-polymarket-npm-crypto-wallet-drainer/
ATT&CKT1547 T1546.016 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")
| where FolderPath has "/.polybot/" or FolderPath has @"\.polybot\"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node", "node.exe", "npm", "npm.exe", "npx", "npx.exe", "yarn", "yarn.exe", "pnpm", "pnpm.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")

| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node", "node.exe", "npm", "npm.exe", "npx", "npx.exe", "yarn", "yarn.exe", "pnpm", "pnpm.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Megalodon CI runner: shell scraping /proc/*/environ for in-memory secrets Installation Medium
Detects shell or coreutils processes reading /proc/*/environ — the credential-harvesting fingerprint used by the Megalodon GitHub Actions payload to scrape every running process's environment variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_*, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, Vault tokens, etc.) on a self-hosted runner. The article explicitly states the payload reads `/proc/*/environ, and PID 1 environment` — a behaviour vanishingly rare in legitimate CI workflows. Rationale: The article explicitly lists "/proc/*/environ, and PID 1 environment" as one of the first data classes the Megalodon harvester collects — that's a unique behavioural string we can pivot on. Combining `/proc/*/environ` access with shell/coreutils parents distinguishes the attack from a developer running `cat /proc/$$/environ` once for debugging. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/megalodon-mass-github-repo-backdooring-ci-workflows/ • https://cybernews.com/security/megalodon-github-5000-repos-backdooring-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1083 T1057 T1212
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ProcessCommandLine has "/environ"
| where FileName in~ ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "cat", "grep", "awk", "find", "xargs", "tr", "strings", "head", "tail")
    or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (ActingProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "/environ")
    or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "/environ")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "cat", "grep", "awk", "find", "xargs", "tr", "strings")
    or TargetProcessName has_any ("cat", "grep", "awk", "find", "xargs", "tr", "strings")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Megalodon CI Runner /proc/*/environ Mass Secret Scrape
id: cd4e5f6a-7b8c-9d0e-1f2a-3b4c5d6e7f8a
description: Detects shell or coreutils processes reading /proc/*/environ on Linux — the credential-harvesting pattern named in the Megalodon CI/CD payload that scrapes every running process's environment block for CI secrets, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS/GCP/Azure credentials, and OIDC tokens injected by GitHub Actions. Legitimate use of /proc/*/environ from a shell is rare outside debugging or forensic tools.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/megalodon-github-attack-targets-5561.html
  - https://safedep.io/megalodon-mass-github-repo-backdooring-ci-workflows/
author: Detection Team
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.discovery
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1083
  - attack.t1057
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/cat'
      - '/grep'
      - '/awk'
      - '/find'
      - '/xargs'
      - '/tr'
      - '/strings'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/proc/'
      - '/environ'
  condition: selection_image and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
  - Forensic / DFIR triage tooling intentionally enumerating process environments
  - Performance diagnostics scripts inspecting a single PID's environ (lower /proc cardinality)
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:*/proc/*/environ* OR @process.executable.path:(/usr/bin/cat OR /bin/cat OR /usr/bin/grep OR /usr/bin/awk OR /usr/bin/find OR /usr/bin/xargs OR /usr/bin/strings)) AND @process.command_line:*environ*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/\/proc\/[^\s\/]+\/environ/
| ImageFileName=/(bash|sh|dash|zsh|cat|grep|awk|find|xargs|tr|strings|head|tail)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine, UserName], function=count())
| count > 0
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/proc/*" Processes.process="*/environ*" (Processes.process_name=bash OR Processes.process_name=sh OR Processes.process_name=dash OR Processes.process_name=zsh OR Processes.process_name=cat OR Processes.process_name=grep OR Processes.process_name=awk OR Processes.process_name=find OR Processes.process_name=xargs OR Processes.process_name=tr OR Processes.process_name=strings) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/proc/*" Processes.process="*/environ*" (Processes.process_name=bash OR Processes.process_name=sh OR Processes.process_name=dash OR Processes.process_name=zsh OR Processes.process_name=cat OR Processes.process_name=grep OR Processes.process_name=awk OR Processes.process_name=find OR Processes.process_name=xargs OR Processes.process_name=tr OR Processes.process_name=strings) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

ATT&CKT1071

DeviceNetworkEvents

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["216.126.225.129"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev"]);
ImNetworkSession

| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)

description: |

    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev")

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0a

    Registry writes under the browser extension policy keys —
    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

description: |

            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'

            - '\Phantom\'

            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
